description: Peptide Patient's Guide — Retrieval Quality Benchmark. Queries test NeuralMind's ability to find the right chapter/section for patient-facing questions about peptide therapy.

queries.question: What exactly is a peptide and how is it different from a protein?
gold_facts: A peptide is a chain of 2-50 amino acids
Proteins are chains of 50+ amino acids
Peptides serve as signaling molecules
Insulin, oxytocin, and glucagon are examples of peptide hormones

queries.question: How does semaglutide work in the body?
gold_facts: Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist
It mimics the natural hormone GLP-1 produced in the gut
It stimulates insulin secretion from the pancreas
It slows gastric emptying and reduces appetite
Natural GLP-1 has a 2-minute half-life; semaglutide lasts about a week

queries.question: How does BPC-157 work and what is its mechanism of action?
gold_facts: BPC-157 is a synthetic peptide derived from a protein in human gastric juice
It acts on multiple pathways — angiogenesis, cell migration, anti-inflammatory
The VEGFR2-Akt-eNOS pathway is the most consistently studied
It has no single established receptor in humans
Evidence is primarily from animal models with no human RCTs

queries.question: What is the difference between FDA approval and PCAC recommendation for peptides?
gold_facts: FDA approval requires Phase 1-3 clinical trials and an NDA/ANDA
PCAC only recommends whether a substance can be used by compounding pharmacies
PCAC inclusion on the 503A Bulks List is NOT FDA drug approval
PCAC voted to recommend 6 peptides for compounding in July 2026
Emideltide was rejected by PCAC

queries.question: How much weight loss can you expect from semaglutide and tirzepatide?
gold_facts: Semaglutide produced 14.9% average weight loss in STEP 1 trial over 68 weeks
Tirzepatide demonstrated superior weight loss compared to semaglutide in a 2025 NEJM trial
Retatrutide achieved up to 24.2% weight loss in Phase 2 at 48 weeks
Participants who stopped semaglutide regained roughly two-thirds of lost weight within a year

queries.question: Why are most peptides injected instead of taken as pills?
gold_facts: Stomach acid and digestive enzymes break down peptides
The digestive system is designed to dismantle proteins into amino acids
Subcutaneous injection bypasses the digestive tract
Oral semaglutide requires a special absorption enhancer
Native GLP-1 has a half-life of about 2 minutes

queries.question: What are the risks of buying peptides from research chemical websites?
gold_facts: Research chemical sites label products 'Not for human consumption' to bypass FDA oversight
No guarantee of purity, sterility, or accurate dosing
Products may contain bacterial contamination, heavy metals, or completely different compounds
503A pharmacies at least operate under state board oversight
Compounding from unregulated sources means you are your own clinical trial

queries.question: What is the black box warning on semaglutide about?
gold_facts: Semaglutide carries a black box warning for thyroid C-cell tumors
Rodent studies showed increased risk of these tumors
Human risk has not been established
People with family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma should not take GLP-1 agonists
Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 is a contraindication

queries.question: Will there be oral peptide options in the future?
gold_facts: Oral semaglutide already exists using absorption enhancer technology
Researchers are exploring oral formulations for peptides previously thought impossible to deliver without injection
The future of peptide therapy will likely involve wider oral options
Nasal delivery can work for peptides targeting the brain via olfactory nerve pathways

queries.question: Does semaglutide help with heart disease?
gold_facts: The SELECT trial followed over 17,000 adults with overweight/obesity and pre-existing cardiovascular disease
Semaglutide reduced major adverse cardiovascular events by 20% compared to placebo
It was the first peptide therapy shown to actively protect the cardiovascular system
It reduced risk of heart attacks and strokes

queries.question: What should I ask my doctor before starting peptide therapy?
gold_facts: Ask if the peptide is FDA-approved for your specific condition or off-label
Ask what tier of clinical evidence supports it — Phase 1 or Phase 3
Ask what the documented long-term risks are and how they will be monitored
Ask about interactions with current medications

queries.question: What percentage of patients experience nausea on semaglutide?
gold_facts: Nausea affects about 44% of patients
Vomiting affects 24% of patients
Diarrhea affects 30% of patients
Side effects are most pronounced when starting or increasing dose

queries.question: Is retatrutide FDA approved?
gold_facts: Retatrutide is not FDA-approved as of mid-2026
It is a triple agonist targeting GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors
Phase 3 trials are ongoing
It achieved up to 24.2% weight loss in Phase 2 trials

queries.question: Are peptides the same as steroids?
gold_facts: Peptides and steroids are not the same
Anabolic steroids are synthetic derivatives of testosterone
Peptides and steroids work through different classes of receptors
Steroids carry risks including liver toxicity and cardiovascular disease
Peptides are biologically different categories of molecules

queries.question: Why do some peptide medications require refrigeration?
gold_facts: Peptides are inherently fragile molecules
Unlike small-molecule drugs like ibuprofen, peptides have bonds designed to be broken by enzymes
Exposure to heat or repeated freeze-thaw cycles can degrade peptides
A vial left in a hot car may contain biologically inert degraded fragments

queries.question: Are longevity peptides like Epitalon and MOTS-c proven to work?
gold_facts: Longevity peptides lack robust human randomized controlled trial data
Many are based on compelling animal models or in-vitro cell studies
Claims about reversing aging or optimizing biological clocks often lack Phase 3 human data
Epitalon activates telomerase which rebuilds telomeres
MOTS-c inhibits the folate cycle and may elevate homocysteine

queries.question: What is the difference between tirzepatide and semaglutide?
gold_facts: Semaglutide is a single GLP-1 receptor agonist
Tirzepatide is a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist
Tirzepatide targets two gut hormones simultaneously
In a 2025 NEJM trial, tirzepatide showed superior weight loss to semaglutide
Semaglutide half-life is about 165 hours; tirzepatide is about 120 hours

queries.question: What should I expect at my first peptide therapy appointment?
gold_facts: You will fill out a detailed health history questionnaire
The clinician will walk through your history and goals
Expect education about how the proposed peptide works
Labs may be ordered to establish baseline values
The first dose may be given in the clinic for observation

queries.question: What is ziconotide approved for?
gold_facts: Ziconotide is FDA-approved for severe chronic pain management
It is delivered via intrathecal infusion into the spinal cord
It is derived from the venom of a marine cone snail
It blocks N-type calcium channels to interrupt pain-signal transmission
